mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 5% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate exceeds 5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises while employment does not fall, it indicates labor market stress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the specified labor market conditions occur but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates increase borrowing costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If federal funds rates are high but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production suggests strong supply chains, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI increase above 210 indicates high inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If CPI exceeds 210 but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 45% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: If GDP growth slows but retail sales increase, consumption-driven growth may occur, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth slows and retail sales rise but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, increased housing starts and low unemployment may signal an impending slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts and unemployment are in the specified range but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.
